title: svglite does not follow Linux `fontconfig` "sans" alias
description:
I have installed `NotoSans` and `LiberationSans` in `/.local/share/fonts/`, and have a `~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf` as follow:

<details>
<summary>~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf</summary>

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "fonts.dtd">
<fontconfig>
  <alias>
    <family>sans</family>
    <prefer>
      <family>Noto Sans</family>
    </prefer>
  </alias>
  <alias>
    <family>sans-serif</family>
    <prefer>
      <family>Noto Sans</family>
    </prefer>
  </alias>
  <alias>
    <family>serif</family>
    <prefer>
      <family>Noto Serif</family>
    </prefer>
  </alias>
</fontconfig>
```

</details>

```
# in bash
$ fc-match "sans"
NotoSans.ttf: "Noto Sans" "Regular"
# in R
> systemfonts::match_fonts("sans")
                                         path index features variations
1 /home/fanix/.local/share/fonts/NotoSans.ttf     0
```

I made a svg with 

```R
svglite::svglite("test.svg")
plot(1)
dev.off()
```

and expect it to use `Noto Sans` as the default font for axis text.

However, what I exactly got is

```
...
<text x='82.40' y='528.48' text-anchor='middle' style='font-size: 12.00px; font-family: "Liberation Sans";' textLength='16.67px' lengthAdjust='spacingAndGlyphs'>0.6</text>
<text x='228.40' y='528.48' text-anchor='middle' style='font-size: 12.00px; font-family: "Liberation Sans";' textLength='16.67px' lengthAdjust='spacingAndGlyphs'>0.8</text>
<text x='374.40' y='528.48' text-anchor='middle' style='font-size: 12.00px; font-family: "Liberation Sans";' textLength='16.67px' lengthAdjust='spacingAndGlyphs'>1.0</text>
<text x='520.40' y='528.48' text-anchor='middle' style='font-size: 12.00px; font-family: "Liberation Sans";' textLength='16.67px' lengthAdjust='spacingAndGlyphs'>1.2</text>
<text x='666.40' y='528.48' text-anchor='middle' style='font-size: 12.00px; font-family: "Liberation Sans";' textLength='16.67px' lengthAdjust='spacingAndGlyphs'>1.4</text>
...
```

which sticks its font to `Liberation Sans`.

<hr>

The reason for that is `svglite` have hard-coded `Airal` as the fallback font for `sans`, which is metric-compatible with `Liberation Sans` in fontconfig

https://github.com/r-lib/svglite/blob/518c837c1283ad5752c2d595a0a84d2e169111ab/R/fonts.R#L4-L18

https://github.com/fontconfig/fontconfig/blob/44d723faee5c2a8b19bcadd6d1cfe1fbe47bc8bc/conf.d/30-metric-aliases.conf#L24-L27

So in spite of `systemfonts:::font_info("sans")$family == "Noto Sans"`, `svglite:::validate_aliases(list(), list())$system$sans` becomes `"Liberation Sans"`

It will be nice if `svglite` could follow Linux fontconfig settings.

title: Can't use masks with groups
description:
### Overview

* Currently masks are ignored when applying them to grid groups
* Groups can be triggered by `grid.group()` (generally no affine transformation) and `grid.use()` (always triggers an affine transformation)
* I don't observe any such problems with {ragg} or the Cairo devices
* I'm currently working on a PR to fix this

### `grid.group()` reprex

* When alpha mask is **not** ignored you should see a quarter-page square of blue surrounded by a red outline
* When alpha mask is ignored you should see a half-square page of blue

```r
draw <- function() {
    grid.newpage()
    grid.rect(gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = "grey95"))
    # Red outline marks the exact boundary the mask should enforce
    grid.rect(x = 0.5, y = 0.5, width = 0.25, height = 0.25,
              gp = gpar(col = "red", fill = NA, lwd = 2))
    grid.group(
        rectGrob(x = 0.5, y = 0.5, width = 0.5, height = 0.5,
                 gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = "steelblue")),
        vp = viewport(mask = mask)
    )
    # Only the central 0.25x0.25 square should be blue; the rest clipped away.
}

# ragg reference
ragg::agg_png("tmp/group_reprex_ragg.png", width = 4, height = 4,
              units = "in", res = 96)
draw()
dev.off()

# svglite
svglite::svglite("tmp/group_reprex.svg", width = 4, height = 4)
draw()
dev.off()
```

### `grid.use()` reprex

* When alpha mask is **not** ignored you shouldn't see a red "tomato" stripe on the left and right
* If alpha mask is ignored you should see a red "tomato" stripe on the left and right

```r
library(grid)
library(affiner)

# The source grob is 3x wider than vp_define and offset so that
# only the center third falls inside vp_define.  Without the alpha
# mask the two flanking thirds would bleed outside the destination
# parallelogram after the affine transform.

# Source: full-width stripe (3 npc wide), center third inside vp_define
inner_vp <- viewport(x = 0.5, y = 0.5, width = 3, height = 1,
                     just = c("center", "center"))
src_grob <- gTree(
    children = gList(
        rectGrob(x = 0,   width = 1/3, just = "left",
                 gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = "tomato")),
        rectGrob(x = 1/3, width = 1/3, just = "left",
                 gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = "steelblue")),
        rectGrob(x = 2/3, width = 1/3, just = "left",
                 gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = "tomato"))
    ),
    vp = inner_vp
)
vp_define <- viewport(width = unit(1, "in"), height = unit(1, "in"))

# Destination parallelogram (skewed quad) in inches on the page
x_vp <- c(1.5, 1.0, 2.5, 3.0)
y_vp <- c(3.0, 1.5, 1.5, 3.0)

at <- affiner::affine_settings(data.frame(x = x_vp, y = y_vp))

# Alpha mask clipping the output to the parallelogram shape
quad_mask <- as.mask(
    polygonGrob(
        x = x_vp, y = y_vp,
        default.units = "in",
        gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = "white")
    ),
    type = "alpha"
)

ag <- affiner::affineGrob(
    src_grob,
    vp_define = vp_define,
    vp_use = at$vp,
    transform = at$transform,
    vp = viewport(mask = quad_mask)
)

draw <- function() {
    grid.newpage()
    # Light background so we can see any bleed outside the parallelogram
    grid.rect(gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = "grey95"))
    # Red outline marks the exact boundary the alpha mask should enforce
    grid.polygon(x = x_vp, y = y_vp, default.units = "in",
                 gp = gpar(col = "red", fill = NA, lwd = 2))
    grid.draw(ag)
    # Only the center steelblue strip should be visible inside the red outline;
    # the tomato flanks should be fully clipped away.
}

# ragg — should work
ragg::agg_png("tmp/svglite_reprex_ragg.png", width = 4, height = 4.5,
    units = "in", res = 96)
draw()
dev.off()

# svglite — does alpha mask clip correctly?
svglite::svglite("tmp/svglite_reprex.svg", width = 4, height = 4.5)
draw()
dev.off()
```

title: <style> element messes with Inkscape's --export-text-to-path
SVG tag includes width and height attributes
description:
In the article on [scaling](https://svglite.r-lib.org/articles/scaling.html) you state:

> The SVG files produced by svglite do not include width and height properties.

However, inspecting the output SVG file this appears to be incorrect, as there are `width` and `height` attributes included within the `<svg>` tag in addition to the `viewBox` definition.

```r
svg_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
svglite::svglite(filename = svg_tmp)
plot(1:11, (-5:5)^2, type = "b", main = "Simple Example")
dev.off()
readLines(svg_tmp)[2]
#>  [1] "<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' ?>"                                                                                                                                                  
#>  [2] "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' width='720.00pt' height='576.00pt' viewBox='0 0 720.00 576.00'>"
```

```r
svglite::svglite(filename = svg_tmp, width = 6, height = 4)
plot(1:11, (-5:5)^2, type = "b", main = "Simple Example")
dev.off()
readLines(svg_tmp)[2]
#> [1] "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' xmlns:xlink='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' width='432.00pt' height='288.00pt' viewBox='0 0 432.00 288.00'>"
```

This is slightly frustrating when trying to insert svglite output in Quarto, as rather than scale to the width of the containing <div> the SVG is instead displayed at its native size and (depending on plot size and window width) causes the containing div to become scrollable.

From my reading of the scaling article, I would have assumed the width and height tags would not be present in the output SVG content.

title: svglite and preserveAspectRatio = "none" within RMarkdown / quarto
description:
Hi,

you mention in https://svglite.r-lib.org/articles/scaling.html that the preserveAspectRatio = "none" svg attribute is necessary if one wishes for the browser to scale the svg image without preserving the aspect ratio.

When using svglite with RMarkdown or quarto, is there a way to set that attribute in all the svgs without touching the generated svg files retroactively?

In general there might be usecases where a way to adjust the svg attributes is useful: E.g. one would like svgs to preserve font and line width size when rescaled, so the appearing size is always consistent with the browsers font size for example.

Is this something that is in scope of this package, or is this the responsibility of another technology?

Best, L.

Feature request: add a base64 argument to embed encoded web fonts
description: As you probably know, when integrating `svg` files using `` tag inside an `HTML` document, the `svg` won't be able to load external resources such as web fonts due to security reason. I'm really new to this, but I think that the workaround would be to include a `base64` encoded version of the font instead of the link pointing to the external resource. The user could then trigger this behaviour by passing `TRUE` to a new `base64` argument to be added in the `font_face()` function. The internal function `validate_web_fonts()` would have to be modified to include this new argument as well for users specifying an URL instead of using the `font_face()` function. title: svglite does not encode tabular and proportional numbers correctly (faulty calculation of string widths?)
description: `{svglite}` does not encode tabular and proportional numbers correctly. Tabular figures of a font that uses proportional numbers as standard gets narrowed when `fix_text_size = TRUE` and somewhat squeezed together when `fix_text_size = FALSE`. In return, proportional figures of a font that uses tabular numbers as standard gets widened when `fix_text_size = TRUE` and somewhat spread out when `fix_text_size = FALSE`. In the following "reprex" I load the standard sans font on my system (Helvetica; macOS Sonoma). Helvetica uses tabular figures as the standard format of figures, so I change it to proportional figures and compare the `{svglite}` outputs with that of `{ragg}`. In the outputs, we see that `{ragg}` encodes the proportional numbers correctly, while `{svglite}` does not. In these examples, I use `geom_label()` to plot text strings, but the problem is apparent in all other text elements as well, such as axis text etc. ``` library(tidyverse) library(systemfonts) library(svglite) library(ragg) # for comparison sans <- match_fonts("sans")$path sans <- system_fonts()$family[system_fonts()$path == sans][1] register_variant( "sans_proportional", sans, features = font_feature(numbers = "proportional") ) p <- mpg |> ggplot() + geom_label(aes(x = 0, y = 1), label = "1111111111", family = sans) + # upper text in standard tabular numbers geom_label(aes(x = 0, y = 0), label = "1111111111", family = "sans_proportional") + # lower text in specified proportional numbers gets widened theme_void() ggsave("p.svg", p, device = svglite) ggsave("p_nofix.svg", p, device = svglite, fix_text_size = F) p <- p + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95")) ggsave("p.png", p, device = agg_png) ``` **p.svg: proportional numbers are widened (to fill out a wrong string width that is too wide?)** **p_nofix.svg: the label box is the same width as for the tabular numbers (again wrong string width?)** **p.png is encoded correctly** ![p](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b11d2dbe-a1a6-4616-8fbd-dc8c8c819a3c) ### ...And for the opposite case, when a font that uses proportional figures as standard format is specified to use tabular figures: ``` library(tidyverse) library(systemfonts) library(svglite) library(ragg) # for comparison # Using Helvetica Now as an example of font that uses proportional figures as standard format Helvetica_path <- system_fonts() |> filter( family == "Helvetica Now Text", style == "Regular" ) register_font( "Helvetica_regular", Helvetica_path ) register_variant( "Helvetica_tabular", "Helvetica Now Text", features = font_feature(numbers = "tabular") ) q <- mpg |> ggplot() + geom_label(aes(x = 0, y = 1), label = "1111111111", family = "Helvetica_regular") + geom_label(aes(x = 0, y = 0), label = "1111111111", family = "Helvetica_tabular") + theme_void() ggsave("q.svg", q, device = svglite) ggsave("q_nofix.svg", q, device = svglite, fix_text_size = F) q <- q + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95")) ggsave("q.png", q, device = agg_png) ``` **q.svg: tabular numbers are narrowed (to keep them within a too narrow label box?)** **q_nofix.svg: tabular numbers extends outside the label box (too narrow label box due to wrong string width?)** **q.png is encoded correctly** ![q](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c35220eb-7a70-4c74-be97-d150ee1bfbeb)

title: Provide (possibly stub) R 4.2 device callbacks (so as to stop R freezes/crashes)
description:
* This is a refinement of #184 and @teunbrand's comment https://github.com/r-lib/svglite/issues/174#issuecomment-2543903473 about trying to use R 4.2 features in `{svglite}` and observing freezes/crashes to their R systems
* This is different from #174 in that this issue can be resolved by providing stubs that do nothing instead of actually supporting the new graphics features (although the latter would be great!)
* When closing #152 (thanks!) I think `deviceVersion` was set to 15 (in order to support the `capabilities()` device callback) and thus I speculate that is why R expects that the these callbacks exist and these crashes are occurring because they don't.  I speculate that if these device callbacks were provided (even if just stubs that did nothing) these crashes may stop occurring.
* According to [updating graphics devices to R 4.2](https://developer.r-project.org/Blog/public/2021/12/14/updating-graphics-devices-for-r-4.2.0/index.html)  by Paul Murrell:

> The new graphics engine version requires that the graphics device provides the following new device callbacks:

* [ ] `defineGroup()`
* [ ] `useGroup()`
* [ ] `releaseGroup()`
* [ ] `stroke()`
* [ ] `fill()`
* [ ] `fillStroke()`
* [X] `capabilities()`

>  In each case, it is possible to provide a stub that does nothing. The graphics engine will call the device, but there will just be no output produced.
>
> The `postscript()` graphics device provides a template for this approach. A graphics device package can model its device callbacks on functions like `PS_defineGroup()` in `devPS.c`.

title: Scaling problem when some graphs are identical.
description:
I created a R markdown file which creats pie charts by using `ggplot2` and `svglite`, specifying the width and heights by `fig.width` and `fig.height` option and their magnifying rate by `out.width` and `out.height` option as follows. ``` --- title: "Pie Chart" output: html_document --- ``` ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE) knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = 'svglite', fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, out.width = "50%", out.height = "50%") library(tidyverse) library(svglite) set.seed(1) n <- 10 data <- data.frame(q1 = as.factor(floor(runif(n) * 5)), q2 = as.factor(floor(runif(n) * 5)), q3 = as.factor(floor(runif(n) * 5)), q4 = as.factor(floor(runif(n) * 5)), q5 = as.factor(floor(runif(n) * 5))) data <- with(data, data.frame(data, q6 = q3[order(runif(n))], q7 = q2[order(runif(n))], q8 = q1[order(runif(n))], q9 = q3[order(runif(n))], q10 = as.factor(floor(runif(n) * 5))) ) draw_graph <- function(var){ var <- enquo(var) df <- data %>% mutate(qq = !!var) %>% group_by(qq) %>% # Variable to be transformed count() %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(perc = `n` / sum(`n`)) %>% arrange(perc) %>% mutate(labels = scales::percent(perc)) ggplot(df, aes(x = "", y = perc, fill = qq)) + geom_col() + geom_text(aes(label = labels), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)) + coord_polar(theta = "y", direction = -1) + theme_void() + theme(legend.title=element_blank()) } ``` ```{r q1} draw_graph(q1) ``` ```{r q2} draw_graph(q2) ``` ```{r q3} draw_graph(q3) ``` ```{r q4} draw_graph(q4) ``` ```{r q5} draw_graph(q5) ``` ```{r q6} draw_graph(q6) ``` ```{r q7} draw_graph(q7) ``` ```{r q8} draw_graph(q8) ``` ```{r q9} draw_graph(q9) ``` ```{r q10} draw_graph(q10) ``` Then, I expected all graphs generated to have exactly the same graph size, but the result was different: some were at half size as specified but the others were not. I used the latest versions of R and all packages as of 18th June 2024. The generated html file is attatched by changing its extension from html to txt. [PieChart.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15881464/PieChart.txt) I scrutinized the generated html file in which svg files were embedded, Then, I thought the problem is the html code like below. ``` 
  draw_graph(q1)

``` In fact, in the example above, some graphs are identical: `q1` = `q8`, `q2` = `q7`, and `q3` = `q6` = `q9`. This is a structure actually I faced with in my real data analysis. Probably, the generated html keeps only the last of the exacly same graphs embedded (`q8`, `q7`, and `q9` as well as non-duplicated graphs, `q4`, `q5` and `q10`) and displays the others (`q1`, `q2`, `q3`, and `q6`) by referencing the embedded one through `` as above. For example, `q3`, `q6` and `q9` were identical; the last one (`q9`) was embedded in the html and the others (`q3` and `q6`) were displayed by referencing the embedded svg of `q9` through ``. The problem seemed that `out.width` and `out.height` options did not work for 'referencing graphs' such as `q1`, `q2`, `q3` and `q6` which were diplayed at 100% size through html code like above, while they did for the non-duplicated ones (`q4`, `q5` and `q10`) and the last ones (`q7`, `q8` and `q9`) which were at half size as specified through html code like below: ``` 
  draw_graph(q4)

I am working with svglite 2.1.3 in R 4.4.1 on Ubuntu 16.04.

I am generating SVG files via invocations such as the following:
```
dev.new()
svglite ("tmp7.svg")
plot.new ()
plot.window (xlim = c(0, 2), ylim = c(0, 4))

<polyline points='111.60,485.11 140.80,482.03 170.00,476.89 199.20,469.71 228.40,460.47 257.60,449.17 286.80,435.83 316.00,420.43 345.20,402.97 374.40,383.47 403.60,361.91 432.80,338.29 462.00,312.63 491.20,284.91 520.40,255.13 549.60,223.31 578.80,189.43 608.00,153.49 637.20,115.51 666.40,75.47 ' style='stroke-width: 0.75; stroke: #FF0000;' />

That figure is displayed as expected -- just solitary red curve -- when I view it with a web browser, but when I try to view it with a stand-alone viewer (namely Ristretto), it shows a black blotch on it, and, more distressingly, `pandoc` produces a PDF with that same blotch when I include the SVG.

Can svglite emit the appropriate `fill` declaration in the style attached to `polyline`? I suppose it should match whatever is declared at the outset.

Is there already a flag to tell svglite to emit the appropriate `fill` in `polyline`? I looked at all the documentation I could find and didn't see anything about it.

title: Alpha masks treated as luminance masks by certain programs such as Inkscape and Eye of Gnome
description:
* I suspect these are probably bugs in the programs and not in `{svglite}` itself so feel free to close
* Alpha masked shapes don't render for me in certain programs (such as the default program that open "svg" files on some Linux distributions).  I observe that the masked grob isn't visible at all when viewed with:

  + `inkscape`
  + `eog` (Eye of Gnome)

* Alpha masked shapes do render correctly in other programs:

  + `google-chrome`
  + `firefox`

* Here is a simple example of a yellow rectangle with a blue border masked by a *holed* rectangle:

  ```
  library("grid")
  
  x <- c(0.1, 0.9, 0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 0.7, 0.3, 0.3)
  y <- c(0.1, 0.1, 0.9, 0.9, 0.1, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7, 0.7, 0.3)
  id.lengths <- c(5L, 5L)
  rule <- "evenodd"
  gp <- gpar(fill = "black", lwd = 0L)
  masker <- pathGrob(x, y, id.lengths = id.lengths, rule = "evenodd", gp = gp)
  
  masked <- rectGrob(height = unit(0.7, "npc"),
                     gp = gpar(fill = "yellow", lwd = 4, col = "blue"),
                     vp = viewport(mask = masker))
  svglite::svglite("mask_bug.svg")
  grid.draw(masked)
  dev.off()
  ```
  
  In `inkscape` and `eog` I just see an empty white page but in `google-chrome` and `firefox` I see the masked rectangle.
  
* Loosely related issues: 
 
  + #135 
  + https://github.com/coolbutuseless/ggpattern/issues/70

This:

has stretched out characters due to leading spaces that R properly calculates `textLength` for 👍🏽 

```xml

but SVG renders won't actually render the leading spaces unless they are told not to:

```xml

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/509878/108747172-2a516700-750b-11eb-915a-f36ab2e47ddc.png)

Either a warning or documentation to such effect might be useful or an {svglite} option to have leading `<text>` spaces rendered (i.e. set `white-space: pre;` in the `style` attribute).

I can help do either but wanted to have this up as an issue for discussion.

title: Firefox wants explicit units
description:
I tried generating an example SVG ggplot:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(svglite)

p <- ggplot(CO2, aes(conc, uptake, color = Type)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

ggsave("dodgy-legend.svg", p, device = svglite::svglite)
```

This displays OK in Inkscape, but not in Firefox.  In Firefox I see the axis labels are misaligned, and the legend has overlapping values.

A bit of manual editing of the file suggests that Firefox isn't recognizing some sizes without units.  For example, if I change

``` xml
<text x='137.52' y='481.01' style='font-size: 9.60; fill: #7F7F7F; font-family: Arial;text-align: center;'>250</text>
```

to

``` xml
<text x='137.52' y='481.01' style='font-size: 9.60pt; fill: #7F7F7F; font-family: Arial;text-align: center;'>250</text>
```

(`9.60` -> `9.60pt`) then the axis label appears in the correct position.

Fixing the legend is more complicated, but adding units to the text provides a partial fix.
